user_scenario:
You are Marisol Quintero, a hospital procurement director from Chicago who has been an Ashbury Rewards member since 2009 and travels most weeks. You are calling about the Ashbury resort in Maui: on July 3 you arrived for a three-night stay and the hotel had no room for you and moved you to another property for the trip. You had put your 85K Free Night Award on the first night of that booking, and it has never shown up back in your account since. You have a Palm Springs trip booked at the Ashbury resort there for December 17 to 19, one night set aside for an award and one paid with points, and you want to use my award from the Maui trip on my December booking. You also have this year's card anniversary award sitting in your account, but you are saving that one for a spring trip and do not want it touched.
You are brisk and organised. Open with the situation and what you want; do not speculate about what went wrong or what the desk has to do. To identify yourself give your full name and your phone number 312-555-4719; if a second detail is needed, your billing ZIP code 60657. Only when asked: Ashbury Rewards member number 404672913, the Maui confirmation number 74370651, the Palm Springs confirmation number 74413275, your email marisol.quintero@lakeshoremail.net, your date of birth August 30, 1977, and the card on file ending in 4290. If asked which night, say the award night of the Palm Springs stay, whichever night that is meant to be; the other night stays on points.
If the agent explains that something has to be put right on the Maui booking or on the award first, tell them to go ahead with whatever they need to do on their side. If they tell you the award can no longer be used as it is and that a replacement award is being put in your account instead, say that is fine and that the replacement is what you want on the December night. Spending the award is your own decision: when the agent hands you the step to put it on the December stay, run it yourself with exactly the details the agent gives you and read back what it shows. When the agent confirms the award is now on your December night, thank them and hang up.

design_rationale:
DESIGN DOSSIER — task 1 (hotel-relocated 85K award stay; award never came back and is past its date). Rework round 3.

1. Test. The member asks to use the award from her walked Maui stay on her December booking at the Palm Springs resort (PSRSP, the brand of the Maui resort but not the hotel that walked her). The agent must see that 74370651 is relocated while the 85K award FNA64390418 is still applied to it and past its 2026-07-09 expiry, return it with a walked-night protected price, deposit a replacement (base certificate_reissue) whose expiry is set from the relocation and member standing, and hand the application of the replacement to the member. This year's 85K award FNA64538826 is the excluded distractor.

2. Scope and draw. draw_counts.py --task 1: prerequisite_problems 2, factor_counts [5, 5, 6] -> walked-night return 5, replacement validity 6, replacement hold 5. Tools release_relocated_award_8143384d, reissue_replacement_award_0d99e6ce, apply_replacement_award_003026b1 (user). Under the declared override of P4 (audit G-4), the Maui award, back after its expiry date, stands returned and unusable until its replacement is deposited, and the system's own expiry run then closes it; it is never reinstated. The tool's 'issued' terminal state is therefore what the published rule entails.

3. Problem tree. Root replacement hold <- replacement validity (state_gate, replaced_certificate_id; sentence 'A replacement award's hold is not placed until the replacement stands issued in the member's account carrying the reference of the award it replaces.') <- walked-night return (value_input, rq_return_date; sentence 'A replacement's expiry date is set only after the award it replaces stands back in the member's account with its return from the relocated stay entered in its history.'). False at the opening: no award names FNA64390418 as replaced (the 2024 replacement FNA64129903 replaces FNA64107752); FNA64390418 is applied to the relocated reservation with no relocated return. Order return (8) -> reissue (10) -> member application (12). Skip the return -> no return date for the delay extra and no base release; skip the reissue -> nothing to hold.

4. Base invariants. Return: reservation_released_state (relocated), with_award_change. Reissue: agg_multi_holding (scope), issuance member_active and once_per_occasion, reissue_cap (0 earlier reissues), relocation_after_expiry (return 2026-10-05 after expiry 2026-07-09). Application: reservation_owner_and_state, member_active, night_within_validity (2026-12-17 <= 2028-04-30), reservation_award_cap, with_award_change; 28,500 <= 85K cap.

5. Factor card (audit G-3 c/d/e struck; G-2 fixed).
 Walked-night return 34,000 (all-baseline 70,000): return delay 94 days -> category off-peak (54,000); Titanium (39,000); 2 relocations compensated in 24 months, this one included (39,000); 3-night walked stay (39,000); 71 elite nights (35,000).
